ACCEPT threshold = 1.14*sigma-hat (null 95th percentile: E[RMS]=0.71sigma under 6pts/3params/df=3, chi^2_3 95th = 7.815), WEAK ceiling = 2.28*sigma-hat; the fixed 0.05 was always this rule at Kaplan sigma (1.14*0.044=0.05); if sigma-hat > 0.07 the fixed 0.05 is void (a perfect fit passes only ~half the time). df=3 boundary: RMS itself is uncertain +-40% (1/sqrt(6)), the ACCEPT/WEAK boundary sits inside a single reading's CI -- RMS is coarse screening only, section 4 sign patterns (p=3.1%, sigma-independent) and profile CIs are the primary judges. Huber caveat: delta=1e-3 at sigma~0.05 makes the fit effectively L1, the chi^2 derivation is an L2 approximation -- within +-0.02 of a threshold, parametric bootstrap with the actual fitter decides (escape hatch pre-registered). sigma-hat measured at 0.2b is a conservative upper bound for the ladder; e1's attn A/B shares the same sigma-hat v1.6 corrects v1.5's direction error: sigma-hat from the smallest point is an UPPER BOUND on the ladder's sigma, but in the ACCEPT rule (RMS <= 1.14*sigma-hat) an over-estimate loosens the threshold -> false ACCEPT -- 'conservative upper bound' was anti-conservative for the verdict. Pre-registered asymmetric reading: ACCEPT carries a 'noise-loose' label (WEAK semantics: interpolation ok, extrapolation banned), FAIL is hard (a true tighter threshold would only make it harder); the sigma-independent judges (section 4 sign patterns p=3.1%, profile CIs) are primary. Thresholds hang on the CONTRIBUTION p_trad*deltaE_script, not the fraction: deltaE_script = per-script val NLL gap (traditional minus simplified) measured directly on the strongest checkpoint (no fertility guessing); <=0.05 nat no action; 0.05-0.10 E's corpus label carries the mix term as uncertainty; >0.10 fertility-correct D (D'=D*(1-p+p/k), k measured from tokenizer) and report both fits, E reported as mixed-corpus floor never model ceiling. facts.value: pre-registered decision tree for what to do after the six points are fit (docs/lessons/scaling_decision_tree.md v1.6, frozen before the points run): three mechanical reads -- doubling gain d_double=(L(Dmax)-E)(1-2^-beta), asymptote gap R=L(Dmax)-E, recognition levels (math twin / minimal pairs / LAMBADA at Dmax) -- drive the branches: d_double>=0.05 and R>0.10 -> extend D; R<0.05 -> data scaling done, read recognition: twin>0.75 + pairs>0.75 + LAMBADA>0.30 + generative<0.02 = recognition ceiling (knowledge present, production absent) -> SFT first, scale N only if SFT fails to move generation; twin<0.60 or pairs<0.60 = knowledge absent -> change data recipe. v1.1 adds the reweight branch (section 2a): triggered when E2 per-domain slope spread max-min > 2xSE and the flattest-slope domain's weight >=10% (web_hq: -0.123 vs textbook/en -0.26, weight 32.4%); anti-trigger = offsets differ but slopes equal (offset is intrinsic entropy, not waste -- never reweight on offsets alone); when d_double<0.05 reweight is the only live data-side action, when >=0.05 reweight goes first (zero new corpus, one mix json) and its result calibrates whether E2 slopes predict reallocation gains. Reweight read pre-registered: same-D old/new mix checkpoints, aggregate val NLL improvement >0.05 = lever holds, <=0.05 = lever retired. Shift capped at 10pt of weight (linearity untested beyond). Identification limit: E2 domains co-varied across the ladder, slopes are ranked observations not causal marginals -- the reweight run IS the experiment. Fixed-N optimum: D* = smallest D with L(D)<=E+0.05 (within noise of the asymptote); the curve values only the 'more data' option, the tree puts alternatives on the same ruler. Fit-failure branches pre-registered (U-shape -> regime boundary, monotone drift -> wrong form, RMS>0.10 -> panel-only decision). Thresholds anchored to run-to-run noise (0.05, Kaplan) and the known-answer calibrations v1.2 adds section 3d (architecture migration of the recognition thresholds, written before the points run): the 0.75/0.75/0.30/0.02 thresholds are absolute claims (twin 0.75 = 3:1 discrimination), old-arch measurements were only feasibility evidence; after the six points, before reading the Dmax branch, re-run known-answer on the new arch's strongest checkpoint -- spread <60pt cuts the metric, reading below the absolute threshold lowers it by the fraction-of-demonstrated-range rule (two-way: 0.5+0.557*(ceiling-0.5), 0.557=(0.75-0.5)/(0.949-0.5); LAMBADA: 0.843*ceiling, 0.843=0.30/0.356; pass@1 stays absolute 0.02), recalibrated numbers frozen before the branch read, weakening reported. Section 6 table now labels every threshold measured/chosen with its source; the four 0.05s declared the same deliberate 1x-noise reuse v1.3 adds the corpus-quality interpretation clause (section 4 supplement, written before the points run): web_hq skipped the top-40% quality-head cut this version, so the six points train on a dirtier corpus than declared. Rules frozen: E is 'this corpus's floor', not 'the model's ceiling' -- no external comparison (Chinchilla 1.69 etc.); R=L(Dmax)-E is immune to ADDITIVE entropy (both terms shift, R unchanged), the misfire risk is only the non-additive case (noise tokens bend the curve flat at smaller D, capacity saturated on noise), unmeasurable until 44's W/F; R<0.05 reads as 'scaling done ON THIS CORPUS'; if section 3b (recognition absent) triggers, dirty corpus is a known suspect and the quality cut is the first recipe-change candidate; beta is immune to a constant noise fraction (D'=c*D absorbed by B only, beta unchanged) -- the warmup overestimate remains the only known beta bias. W/F is the pre-registered falsifier: E_W < E_dirty-0.05 -> floor was inflated, tree re-walked on W curve; R_W>0.10 where R_dirty<0.05 -> non-additive flattening confirmed, extend-D reopens on clean corpus; both within 0.05 -> the cut is worth ~0 at this scale. fb's intuition that 'R is compressed by entropy' was refined in the clause: additive entropy cancels in R. v1.6 flags the steep pole as single-source: textbook/en (both -0.26) share the source chinese-cosmopedia (en domain is 85% Chinese, cause traced to build_domains.sh:32 merging cosmopedia_extra.jsonl + en_textbook.jsonl, container label read as language label) -- the slope spread's steep end is one source counted twice, not two independent witnesses; trigger reading unchanged, reweight direction argument narrowed to 'web_hq -> cosmopedia'

facts.value: pre-registered read rules for e1's KDA vs full-attention A/B (docs/lessons/attn_ab_read_protocol.md, frozen before results): arms --attn_every 1 (12x GatedMLA, 194M) vs --attn_every 4 (9 KDA + 3 GatedMLA, 206M, +5.8%), 4 seeds x 2 arms at 0.2b. (1) MDE: e1's 0.035 is irreproducible -- it assumes seed SD s=0.015 but internal seed variance has never been measured (only anchor: Kaplan 0.05 -> MDE 0.12); frozen rule is self-calibrating: threshold = 2.371*s_pooled from the 8 runs' own seed spread (t_0.975,6+t_0.8,6)*sqrt(2/4), with the df=6 uncertainty band [0.64s, 2.20s] reported -- gap inside the band = no resolution. (2) Primary metric = aggregate val NLL (one number, same quantity as the scaling fit); all 7 per-domain NLLs are secondary diagnostics, all reported, cherry-picking banned, decision claims need Bonferroni 0.05/7. (3) Panel secondaries (CLiMP/LAMBADA/math v2) are trend-only at 0.2b, not in the decision, unless between-arm spread > metric MDE AND readings above floor+MDE. Decision tree: full-attention wins >= threshold -> ladder switches to attn_every 1 (timing fb's call -- switching mid-ladder mixes architectures); KDA wins >= threshold -> unreadable alone (capacity confound is binary, margin size does not resolve it), mandatory balance arm --ffn_hidden 3392 with param counts verified from run logs within +-1%; |gap| < threshold -> KDA stays, '0.2b no resolution', re-ask at 3.24b on the ladder's own checkpoints (e1's original 'no sig diff -> delete KDA' violates the empty-cell rule, void) Scheduling and gate added 2026-08-30 (fb scheduling, gate threshold pre-registered here): step 1 runs 4x attn_every 4 seeds unconditionally (24 min; seed 0 = ladder's 0.2b point, spread = sigma-hat df=3, 44's F arm); step 2 computes MDE = 2.371*s_4; GATE: MDE <= 0.08 -> run 4x attn_every 1 (0.08 = ceiling of the realistic 0.01-0.05 arch-gap range at 200M/0.2b; an MDE past the ceiling can only produce a predictable 'no resolution', waste), MDE > 0.08 -> defer the whole A/B to 3.24b (free re-ask on ladder checkpoints). The sigma-hat CI (df=3, factor 6.5x) does NOT enter the gate: at MDE_point=0.08 the probability true MDE <= 0.08 is ~50%, the band cannot move the gate informatively -- using it would be noise-as-information; the CI's job is in the read (gap inside [1.52s, 5.22s] = no resolution). Timing ruling (fb): the A/B fully completes before the ladder starts -- no mid-ladder arch switch ever; if it ever arises, finish the current arch and re-run the whole curve on the other (a mixed-arch curve is not a bad curve, it is a meaningless one)

facts.value: sampled audit of facts currency (docs/lessons/facts_audit_2026-08-30.md): 20 measured facts sampled seed 20260830 from a population of 98, criteria pre-registered before sampling (C1 arch anchor on old-arch unlabeled, C2 stale corpus state, C3 changed code defaults treated as actual). 1/20 stale (5%, Wilson 95% CI [0.9%, 23.6%]): ds.trainpy_steps computed 254 steps/0.2b point from train.py defaults (6 GPU/batch 32/accum 1) while the ladder actually runs 7 GPU/batch 16/accum 2 = 218 steps -- the default-as-actual error class again, evidence it is systemic not one-off; fixed (defaults vs ladder_actual split). The other 19 hold: 9 mlm.src.* external metadata (version-pinned, cannot expire by construction), tokenizer/contamination/data-quality measurements anchor fixed datasets, eff.* facts anchor the new arch. Limitation: 45% of the sample is external metadata; among the 11 stale-capable facts the rate is 1/11 ~9%. No evidence of mass staleness -- the six-point reading will not cite a batch of dead anchors. Recommendation to de (not applied): facts_well_formed checks field presence not currency; add a soft warning for measured facts whose config carries old-arch markers without an OLD-arch-only label
